root_cause.text: The `__do_adjtimex()` function incorrectly references the core timekeeper (`tk_core`) to update the leap state instead of using the specific auxiliary timekeeper (`tkd`) passed as a parameter, causing both incorrect state updates and lock violations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the line `tk_update_leap_state_all(&tk_core);` to `tk_update_leap_state_all(tkd);`, directly fixing the hardcoded reference. The CVE description confirms that this reference was not updated when `__do_adjtimex()` was made reusable for auxiliary timekeepers, and the lock debugging warning shows the sequence lock write without the proper spinlock.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug in __do_adjtimex where leap state update was incorrectly applied to the global timekeeper instead of the shadow copy when the clock is not being set.
intent_record.what: Changed the argument of tk_update_leap_state_all from &tk_core to tkd in the else branch of __do_adjtimex.
intent_record.how: Previously, the leap state update was applied to the global timekeeper core; now it is applied to the local shadow timekeeper (tkd), ensuring consistency with other updates in the function.
